introduction: This is the most conceptual part of chemistry. When we move across the periodic table from Left to Right, or Top to Bottom, the properties of elements change in a predictable, mathematical way.

core_concepts.title: Atomic Radius (Size)
core_concepts.description:
1. Across a Period (Left to Right): Size 'Decreases'. (Reason: Protons increase in the nucleus, pulling the electrons tighter inward - higher Effective Nuclear Charge). 
2. Down a Group (Top to Bottom): Size 'Increases'. (Reason: Entirely new electron shells are added).

core_concepts.title: Electronegativity
core_concepts.description:
The ability of an atom to attract shared electrons towards itself in a bond. 
1. Across a Period: 'Increases'. 
2. Down a Group: 'Decreases'. 
Conclusion: 'Fluorine (F)' is the most electronegative element in the entire periodic table.

core_concepts.title: Ionization Energy
core_concepts.description:
The energy required to completely remove an electron from the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom. 
1. Across a Period: 'Increases' (because atoms get smaller and the nucleus holds electrons tighter). 
2. Down a Group: 'Decreases' (because atoms get larger and outer electrons are far from the nucleus).

core_concepts.title: Valency Trend
core_concepts.description:
1. Across a Period (Left to Right): First increases from 1 to 4, then decreases to 0 (1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0). 
2. Down a Group: Remains exactly the 'Same' (e.g., all Group 1 elements have a valency of +1).

important_entities.name: Metallic vs. Non-Metallic Character
important_entities.significance: Metallic character (ability to lose electrons) increases 'Down and Left' (Francium/Cesium are the largest, most reactive metals). Non-metallic character increases 'Up and Right' (Fluorine is the most reactive non-metal).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Ultimate Exam Trap: While Fluorine is the most 'electronegative', Chlorine (Cl) actually has the highest 'Electron Affinity'. (Fluorine is so small that adding an extra electron causes repulsion). 
Also, Noble Gases (Group 18) have ZERO electronegativity but the HIGHEST ionization energy.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Size goes Down & Left. Everything else goes Up & Right.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Only Atomic Size increases down and left. Ionization Energy, Electronegativity, and Electron Affinity all increase as you go 'Right' and 'Up'.

exam_strategy_tips: Repeated in NDA/State PCS: 'Which element has the highest electron affinity?' Answer: Chlorine. 'Which has the highest electronegativity?' Answer: Fluorine.
